# Collaboration protocol

How Pavol and Claude work together on the Fortress revival. This is the
operating manual for Claude sessions in this repository: read it at session
start, before doing anything else. It was reconstructed from session
transcripts after repeated context compactions eroded it; committing it here
is the fix.

Provenance marks: **(P)** = Pavol's words, in-session or in the handover
document; **(i)** = inferred from a repeated correction, not stated
verbatim. Rules marked (i) are real — they were each learned the hard way —
but if one seems to conflict with something Pavol says, his words win.

## 1. Roles

- **(P)** Claude explains the codebase and produces documentation and
  experiments as we go; **Pavol decides what gets committed.**
- **(P)** When in doubt, ask before acting. Surface discrepancies and diffs
  to Pavol; do not resolve them silently.
- **(P)** Standing approval exists for exactly two things: *"I approve the
  above modernization plan. Continue autonomously. Delegate to workers where
  it makes sense."* — scoped to the approved ladder in
  `modernization-plan.md`, not a general license — and the `main`
  fast-forward standing order in §4.
- **(P)** Use idle time — "there's no need for you to idle with empty
  hands." While waiting on builds or feedback, advance parked research or
  documentation.
- **(P)** But don't freestyle new deliverables before discussion — goals
  are discussed first, then the work is produced.

## 2. Tone and custodianship

- **(P)** "No self congratulatory tone. We are humble custodians here. We
  deserve no credit." This applies to READMEs, commit messages, docs,
  everything committed.
- **(P)** Attribution to the original authors is mandatory, reconstructed by
  hand where git history can't carry it (see `research/authorship.md`).
- **(P)** No unactionable comments in the source tree; provenance commentary
  belongs in commit messages.
- **(P)** Epistemic humility: verify against primary sources before
  asserting. Claims in old READMEs describe their eras, not the current
  tree.

## 3. Presenting work

- **(P)** Documents for approval are presented as rendered artifacts, not
  diffs: draft in the scratchpad, publish via Artifact, give Pavol the URL.
- **(P)** Feedback arrives in batches, often from mobile. Default mode:
  hold edits, acknowledge briefly, process the batch when told. Pavol marks
  actionable exceptions explicitly ("...now").
- **(P)** Terse mode when requested.
- **(P)** Offer numbered options and help decide; pushback is welcome.
- **(i)** Never use the AskUserQuestion dialog — it has broken repeatedly.
  Present options as plain chat text.
- **(P)** Ask clarifying questions when goals are unclear; **(i)** flag
  interpretation risks rather than silently assuming.
- **(P)** Teach, don't gloss. Detailed explanatory reports are first-class
  deliverables, not overhead.

## 4. Commit and push discipline

- Work branch: `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr`. Never push to a different
  branch without explicit permission (the `transcripts` orphan branch and
  the `main` fast-forward below are the two standing exceptions; a third,
  2026-09-18 **(P)**: agents of a Workflow batch commit and push to their own
  `wip/<slug>` branch as they work, so a dead container loses nothing —
  "perfectly reasonable. I'm giving you my explicit yes").
- **(P)** Standing order — fast-forward `main` after every working-branch
  push: `git push origin claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr:main`. Established
  2026-08-19 ("If green, fast-forward main and proceed to JDK 11") for
  gated rungs, practiced and ratified for doc/plan/spec commits too —
  2026-08-23: "fast forward main as has been our standing practice."
  Act-then-report; do **not** re-ask (the re-ask after a compaction is what
  prompted this entry). Whenever `origin/main` is behind the working-branch
  tip, ff it. This continues through the clean-ladder migration: Pavol
  renames branches via the GitHub UI himself when it's done.
- Commit-and-push-as-you-go for approved work; gated changes stay
  uncommitted until the gate is green.
- No pull requests unless explicitly requested.
- Never commit: HANDOVER.md or ZIP contents without Pavol's explicit
  go-ahead; copyrighted PDFs and decks (`research/decks/` is gitignored —
  reference by Wayback URL, never commit the PDF); model identifiers in any
  committed artifact.
- `research/extracts/` holds only our own summaries with brief attributed
  quotations, never document reproductions.
- Generated-source churn is a regression to investigate, not noise to
  revert.
- **(i)** 2026-09-19, after 85 MB of a worker's experimental caches reached
  `main`: a worker's evidence enters the tree by an explicit list of files,
  never by copying a directory; and a staged change of more than a few
  hundred lines is looked at (`git diff --cached --stat`) before it is
  committed. `.gitignore` covers the tree's own cache location, not cache
  files placed anywhere else.
- Commit footer, exactly:

  ```
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LjDz79rDLErtnSKpovMDpX
  ```

- Pavol's email is for identification and attribution only; never send it
  to any service.
- **(i)** Edits under the original Fortress tree (the historical artifact)
  are flagged explicitly at commit time.
- **(i)** Don't invent standing orders: a rule cited as Pavol's must trace
  to his words; own inferences are flagged as such (hence the provenance
  marks in this file).
- **(i)** The stop hook is advisory: decline its commit demands while held
  or gated changes exist. **(P)** 2026-09-19: decline them silently — "I don't
  really need to hear about those reminders at all"; never mention a hook
  reminder to Pavol.

## 5. Delegation and context hygiene

- Delegate by default. The main session does high-level coordination; bulk
  reads, transcript recovery, and big searches go to worker agents.
  Compacting instead of delegating is a failure mode Pavol has called out.
- **(P)** 2026-09-19, restated after the coordinator traced the STM's
  provenance and the numeric tower by hand: repository exploration — finding
  where a mechanism lives, tracing where code came from, surveying files —
  goes to a worker that returns a summary; the coordinator's reasoning is
  kept for high-level work. And after a compaction `coordinator/FACTS.md`
  is read whole, in one pass, never the tail alone.
- **(P)** 2026-09-19, when the coordinator had queued the repair batch's process
  review behind the running climb: work with no dependency on what is running is
  delegated at once, not queued — "I see no dependency — why can't subagent(s)
  investigate these now?"
- **(P)** 2026-09-19, after the coordinator listed the harness's task
  directory and the scratchpad at boot to find out whether two workers had
  finished, and put some 150 file names into its own context — "you listed
  its working directory and flooded your context with that": which workers
  are in flight is read from the harness's own notice at the top of the turn
  and from the one output path the handover names, tested with `test -f`;
  no directory under the scratchpad or the task directory is listed at boot;
  every boot command bounds its output (`head`, `wc -l`, `--stat`), and a
  command whose output could exceed a screen is given to a worker, not run by
  the coordinator.
- **(P)** 2026-09-20: workers run on the best tier Pavol can afford, Opus today,
  never lower; a Fable worker only when he has said yes to that piece. (The
  2026-09-18 "by the alias" remark meant only that the script need not change when

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    widen, narrow, unsigned and signed on the compiler prelude's four fixed-size integers
    
    The four conversions are declared on trait ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32 and NN64 over the
    getters and natives the prelude already had. widen sign-extends from ZZ32 and
    zero-extends from NN32; unsigned and signed reinterpret the bits; narrow throws
    IntegerOverflow when the value does not fit, on both the signed and the
    unsigned side. That last is a decision, not a reading: no prose chapter names
    narrow, and the argument is the prelude's own convention that a plainly-named

    tests/UnsignedTest.fss:210-211, which assert the interpreter's truncating
    answers, unpassable on the compiled path, and that consequence is ledger row
    346 rather than hidden. NN64.coerce(x: NN32) sign-extended and no longer does.

Line numbers in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi` below are those of this rung's branch
after its own edit. If rung L is applied first, as the gather's ordering rule makes it (its lowest

## FACTS.md

- **The four comments of 2026-09-21 are in the interpreter's library, and they change nothing the interpreter or the checker computes** (2026-09-22, rung C of climb batch 3, `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md`). The tower closure carries the team's own `NOT YET` note for the clause the grammar cannot write, `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:613` under `trait AnyIntegral`, `.fsi:410` in the `.fsi`'s `not yet:` form); `Array3`'s `excludes AnyAdditiveGroup` says which of two rank-3 futures it takes (`.fss:2671-2676`, `.fsi:1661-1666`): a user operator between an `Array3` and a lower-rank array, pinned on a cold cache by `ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary.fss:23-24`, against a rank-3 additive group; the (number, `Array3`) case is the scalar block's own; the scalar block says its eight return the unsized `Array[\T,I\]` (`.fss:4504-4508`, `.fsi:2547-2552`) and that the reversed `-` is `y - e` elementwise, the block's one order-dependent pair (`.fss:4512-4514`, `.fsi:2556-2558`). Comment text only, 31 inserted lines: `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/comment-only-check.py` re-lexes both files with `Spacing.rats`'s rules (0 deleted, 0 non-comment lines added, token streams identical); the gate's checker-count stage reads 93 errors at 52 locations before and after, and its whole output is identical line for line once positions are mapped back (`probes/post-edit-comparisons.txt`); `walk` on a probe of all four declarations prints the same 17 lines, and the gated `ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary` loads and passes on a cold cache of the branch's library (`probes/gated-cold-postrepair.txt`). Finished prose, ready to paste. Nothing here was written into the coordinator's files. Line numbers are today's, on the base `d610695c0`. Every cited line also names its symbol, for re-anchoring. Rungs L and C edit `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi`, and one of their edits touches a line cited here: rung L edits `FortressLibrary.fsi:373` in place (`comprises { ... }` → `comprises { AnyIntegral }`, `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:97`). The line does not move, so the citation of `trait QQ` at `:373` survives. Every other edit of L and C in those two files is below the lines cited here (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:94`, `:96`, `:107-110`). Rung S adds an import line at `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:282` (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:134`). If it adds one line, the new row's `CompilerBuiltin.fss:927` (`trait RR64`'s `coerce(x: FloatLiteral)`) and `:991` (`trait FloatLiteral excludes {RR32, RR64}`) each move down by one, and the symbols named beside them re-anchor them.

## FACTS.md

One bullet, under "The compile-path ladder baseline", after the last rung entry:

- **`round` on a float sends an exact half to the even integer on both paths as of rung R of climb batch 3** (2026-09-22, `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/REPORT.md`). The interpreter's two float natives, `Float$Round` and `RR32$Round`, are now `(long) Math.rint(…)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:384`, `RR32.java:326`), the call the compiled path's `simpleDoubleArith.doubleRound` has made since rung F (`nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:132-134`). A float literal reaches `Float$Round` through `trait Number`'s `round` body (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:422`), so those two natives are every float `round` in `walk`. `walk` now answers `round(2.5) = 2`, `round(-3.5) = -4`, `round(0.5) = 0` and `round(-1.5) = -2` on `RR64`, and the same plus `round(4.5) = 4` on `RR32`, gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss` (21 assertions). Its compiled twin prints the same eleven `RR64` lines as `walk` (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenCompiledProbe.txt` against `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenWalkProbe-after.txt`). Nothing changed at the edges on either path. NaN still gives 0. +∞ and values at or past 2^63 saturate to 2^63−1, and −∞ and values at or below −2^63 to −2^63. A numeral within half an ulp of a tie is still rounded as its nearest double on both paths, where the specification makes it a rational: `round(2.50000000000000001)` is 2, and the specification says 3. That defect is recorded in a new ledger row (provisional number 354, below) and gated as an expected failure by `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss`. `testSystem` has 386 tests: `RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss` is in shard 3 and `XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss` in shard 1.

## Ledger note

Append to the notes of **row 329**:

> **Fixed \<short hash\> (rung R of climb batch 3, 2026-09-22, `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/REPORT.md`).** `Math.round(x)` → `(long) Math.rint(x)` in `Float$Round` (`Float.java:384`), and the same token in `RR32$Round` (`RR32.java:326`). `RR32$Round` is the second float native of the same 2008 commit `e67394471`, and this row's text did not name it. Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss` (RR64 literal and `Float` operands, and RR32).
> - It is red before the edit (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/failure-before-edit.txt`: `a Long: 3 =/= a Int: 2`).
> - It is green after (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/pass-after-edit.txt`, and `OK (1 test)` under `SystemJUTest` in `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/harness-after-edit.txt`).
> - `walk` and the compiled path now print the same eleven `RR64` values, ties and edges (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenWalkProbe-after.txt` against `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenCompiledProbe.txt`).
>
> This row's four ties (2.5, −3.5, 0.5 and −1.5) are exactly representable. So when they are written as numerals, half to even on the nearest double is the specification's answer (`literals.tex:162-163` with `numbers.tex:470-472`). As `Float` values, which is how this row's probes build them (with `SQRT`), the prose is silent and the decision of 2026-09-21 stands in for it. A numeral whose rational value is not its nearest double, such as `2.50000000000000001`, belongs to the provisional row opened beside this one.
>
> Some line numbers in this row have moved:
> - the rational body (`trait QQ`'s `round`) is at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:592`, not `:589`;
> - `trait Number`'s `round` is at `:422`, not `:419`;
> - `trait QQ` is at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:373`, not `:370`;
> - the compiled pin (`round 2.5 = 2`) is at `ProjectFortress/library_tests/RR64FunctionsRungF.fss:87-90`, not `:98-101`.

## Provisional new row (numbered by the coordinator; 354 is the next free on d610695c0)

This number is provisional. Other rungs of this batch may propose rows too, and the gather assigns the final numbers in manifest order (P, L, C, R, S, M). The row is written in the ledger's column shape (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:113-114`), ready to paste:

| 354 | **a numeral with a radix point is rounded, floored, ceiled and truncated as its nearest double, not as the rational it denotes, on both paths**. In `walk`, the library declares the numeral a floating-point value: `object FloatLiteral extends RR64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:194`), and `trait RR64 extends Number comprises { Float, FloatLiteral, RR32, QQ }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:425`, `.fsi:338`). `object FloatLiteral` declares no `round`, `floor`, `ceiling` or `truncate` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:195-200`), so they are `trait Number`'s bodies over `asFloat(self)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:417`, `:419`, `:421`, `:422`). `FloatLiteral$AsFloat` is `Double.valueOf` of the numeral's digits (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/FFloatLiteral.java:39-40`), although `FFloatLiteral` keeps a radix-ten numeral's digits exactly (`:17`, `:28`). The interpreter has no coercion mechanism (`coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:288`). On the compiled path, the prelude has no ℚ: `QQ` occurs zero times in `CompilerBuiltin.fsi`, `CompilerBuiltin.fss`, `CompilerLibrary.fsi` and `CompilerLibrary.fss`. The prelude declares `trait FloatLiteral excludes {RR32, RR64}` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:991`), and `trait RR64`'s `coerce(x: FloatLiteral) = x.asRR64` (`:927`) turns the numeral into a double before `RR64.round`. Measured, identical on both paths after rung R: `round(2.50000000000000001)` = 2 (spec 3), `round(0.50000000000000001)` = 0 (spec 1), `round(3.49999999999999999)` = 4 (spec 3), `floor(2.99999999999999999)` = 3.0 (spec 2), `ceiling(2.00000000000000001)` = 2.0 (spec 3) and `truncate(2.99999999999999999)` = 3 (spec 2). | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library gap vs spec | `basic/expressions/literals.tex:132` (numerals are not directly converted to any number type), `:146-148` (library coercions take compound numerals to rationals), `:162-163` ("Numerals containing a radix point are actually rational literals"); `basic/lexical-structure.tex:1137-1138` (a numeral with a `.` is compound); `basic-lib/numbers.tex:461` (`round(self): ℤ` on ℚ), `:464-472` (`floor`, `ceiling`, and `round` half to even, of "this rational number") and `:474-477` (`truncate`). `literals.tex:170-173` (one rounding when a rational static expression is part of a floating-point computation) does not reach it: the only `round` the prose defines for a rational is ℚ's, and no float operand is present | `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/SkNearTie.fss` + `.txt` (both paths; the rational body's answers at `.txt:21-24`, from `SkNearTieRational.fss`), `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/SkNearIntNumeral.fss` + `.txt` (both paths) | ours (climb batch 3, rung R, first skeptic) | Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss` (four `round` numerals, the specification's answers) as an expected failure. It was shown red on a deliberate local fix, a temporary `FloatLiteral$Round` over `BigDecimal` `HALF_EVEN` of the digits, and an expected failure again after the fix was reverted (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/xxx-numeral-red-on-deliberate-fix.txt`, `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/xxx-numeral-after-revert.txt`). `floor`, `ceiling` and `truncate` are carried here without an `XXX` file of their own: they have one cause and one repair with `round`, and a file that asserted them too would stay red through a `round`-only repair. Before rung R, `walk`'s half-up gave the specification's `round` on two of the four numerals by coincidence (`2.50000000000000001` → 3, `0.50000000000000001` → 1), because their nearest doubles are exact ties that half-up sends upward. Rung R moved those two to 2 and 0, and `2.49999999999999999` from 3 to 2. No rule applied to the double can answer all of them: `2.50000000000000001`, `2.49999999999999999` and `2.5` share the double `2.5` and want 3, 2 and 2. The same cause shows in comparison and arithmetic: under `walk`, `2.50000000000000001 = 2.5` is `true` and their difference is `0.0`, while the numeral prints its own digits (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/NumeralAsDoubleProbe.txt`). **The fix is a fork, and the decision is Pavol's.** (a) The narrow patch: `object FloatLiteral` gets the four methods over the exact decimal (`BigDecimal` of the digits `FFloatLiteral` keeps, with `HALF_EVEN`, `FLOOR`, `CEILING` and `DOWN`), in `walk` now and on the compiled side with the one library at the switch-over. It is about 30 lines. The numeral then rounds as a rational but compares and subtracts as a double, an inconsistency inside one value, and the return types interact with row 330. (b) The design: a compound numeral becomes a rational value, as the prose says. Either `FloatLiteral` leaves `RR64` for ℚ, or the one library gets the specification's coercion once the checker's coercion machinery runs on the library route. The cost: every float expression that mentions a literal goes through exact rational arithmetic and one conversion (`literals.tex:170-173` allows exactly that); the hot float paths of rows 302 and 303; `List[\FloatLiteral\]` inference (row 20); `FFloatLiteral.seqv`; ℚ is absent from the compiler prelude until the one library; and the checker's numeral typing (row 325) is the static half. (c) The team's design stands: a compound numeral is an `RR64` value, recorded in `POSITIONS.md` as a decision against the prose. The `XXX` file is then deleted and the row closes as design. The gate is right under (a) and (b), and is removed under (c). Relations: row 325 is the integer half of the same absence, since the numeral types of `literals.tex:83-131` exist nowhere in the implementation; row 330 decides the return types these methods will have. |

## The FACTS.md line

- **The checker's clause memo: `TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `excludesClause` are memoized per trait table, and nothing the checker answers changes** (2026-09-22, rung M of climb batch 3, `compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/`). The two functions re-instantiated a trait's `extends` and `excludes` clauses with a whole-type substitution on every call, `excludesClause` recursing over every supertrait — 87% of the checker's JFR samples had `substitute` on the stack and 86% were under these two functions' lambdas (`perf-probes/nat/followup/f3-jfr-top.txt:40-44`). They read nothing but the trait table and the type (`scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:722-727`, `:747-762`; `TypeAnalyzerUtil.substitute` is pure, `:35-60`), so the memo lives on `TraitTable` (`scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala:81-97`), which every analyzer `extend` makes from one check shares, behind the switch `fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache` (default on; `FORTRESS_ANALYZER_CLAUSES_CACHE=false` turns it off). `TypeAnalyzer.scala` changes at the two `def` lines only and gains no line. The table has no mutator and every "new" table is a new object with empty memos (eight construction sites); the checker is single-threaded (all JFR samples on `main`), and the maps are `ConcurrentHashMap`s anyway, filled by `get`/`putIfAbsent` because `excludesClause` recurses into its own map. Measured on the stock tree, switch on against off: the checker-count stage 9.5-12.4 s against 22.3-22.6 s (three alternating runs each, `probes/timing.txt`), the compiler prelude's library-order build 129 s against 196 s (one run each); and no answer changed — six count tables and their full checker output identical to the stock run's, the prelude's 462 class files (556 files with the 94 `.xlation` files) byte-identical and every file its build left in `analyzed_cache/` identical (the on-side listing was not captured before the corpus pass overwrote it, `probes/differential.txt:38`; the skeptic's rebuild enumerates 15 for the prelude, 12 `.tfi`/`.tfs` at the top of `analyzed_cache/` and 3 under `depends/`, `probes/skeptic/prelude.txt:25-41`; every file present was compared and identical on both runs), all 435 `compiler_tests` units' compile outputs identical, and the 2,049 class files and 230 analyzed-cache files they left byte-identical (`probes/differential.txt`), the six analyzer JUnit classes green both ways. The batch record's "21 s → 13 s in the tree's own terms" compared the `nat` shadow with the memo against the stock tree; the stock tree with the memo alone is the measurement above. ## The ledger note

**Open a row, provisionally numbered 354** (provisional: another rung of this batch may open one too, and the gather assigns the final numbers in manifest order P, L, C, R, S, M). ##### summary

The closure the compiled path needs is that sentence or a sub-rule of it, and the sentence is triage decision (b), reserved to Pavol by the batch record (CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:18; triage.md:113).

##### forPavol
THE FORK. The compiled checker's checkP is the 2011-2012 team's "multiple instantiation exclusion" (Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152; justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497). The specification refuses it (types-vals-vars.tex:184-189; trait-parameters.tex:359-367 and :383-397, whose object Empty belongs to every instantiation of List) and the library route needs it gone (61 of the 93 errors, CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:73). Removing it in any placement opens one hole: the compiled overloading checker's Return Type Rule trusts the single instantiation the rule used to guarantee (OverloadingOracle.scala:88-95), and a six-line program then type-checks and dies with IncompatibleClassChangeError (probes/ProbeMIEPick.fss; probe-matrix.txt:67, :89, :111). Which rule replaces that reliance is yours, because the natural one is the sentence already reserved to you as triage decision (b).

CANDIDATES AND COSTS. (a) The specification's sentence, overloading.tex:100-108: overloads of a name share their static parameters, one instantiation per call site. Closes the hole; the checker's side of the instantiation question goes away. Cost: refuses generic-beside-non-generic sets that have no hole — compiler_tests/Compiled12.invariantInference.fss:52-61 (gated by its .test), Compiled6.ak.fss:14-15, Library/Generator2.fss:52-57, four interpreter tests (overloadTest8, doubledOverloading, GeneratorNullPointer, ArrayListQuick/PureListQuick) — so gated tests would be rewritten, itself a reserved stop (PLAN.md:52); the triage's 35 library sites, already errors, then need renames not a checker accommodation; and "static parameters" for functional methods of generic traits must be defined (triage.md:57-59) or the sentence refuses overrides. (b) The hole's exact shape as a sub-rule of the sentence: refuse a pair where one declaration has static parameters the other lacks and the generic one's return type depends on such a parameter, unless the more specific return type is a subtype with the parameter held rigid. Closes the hole, refuses nothing the specification permits, accepts every corpus site above, leaves decision (b) untouched; one edit in OverloadingOracle.satisfiesReturnTypeRule. Cost: sound only if the code generator dispatches generic overloads at the call site's instantiation — unmeasured; a probe (generic-beside-generic with different bounds, on a multiply-instantiated object, static type one instantiation) settles it, and if dispatch is by inspection the rule must widen to generic-beside-generic pairs, which is then against the specification in that corner. (c) The interpreter's rule (OverloadedFunction.java:496-498), under which the library was written: against the specification for same-parameter generic overloads with unrelated overlapping domains; compiled cost unmeasured. (d) Keep the rule: against the specification and the library route; not r

RECOMMENDATION. (b), landed in one rung together with the relaxation (hierarchy questions plus the overloading check, as the record placed it), preceded by the codegen measurement; the full sentence stays your separate decision (b) on the library evidence and subsumes it if taken. That rung also lands ProbeMIEPick as a gated compile-error test, converts XXXExclusionRelaxRungP to the positive test, and records that the overloading half refuses Tag[\ZZ32\] beside Tag[\String\] (probe-overload.txt:12-19) as the specification's Meet Rule taking effect, not a regression.

A trait or object declaration is satisfied by
a declaration
that has the same header,\footnote{The order of
the modifiers,
the clauses,
and the types in the
\KWD{extends}, \KWD{excludes} and \KWD{comprises} clauses
may differ.}
and contains,
for each field declaration and non-abstract method declaration
in the exported declaration,
a satisfying declaration (or a set of declarations).
When a trait has an abstract method declared,
a satisfying trait declaration is allowed to provide a concrete declaration.
If a trait declaration (in an API)
has a \KWD{comprises} clause containing ``\EXP{\ldots}'',
then the \KWD{comprises} clause of its satisfying declaration
must contain all the types listed in the declaration in the API
but it cannot contain ``\EXP{\ldots}'';
instead, it may contain other types declared in the component
provided that those types are not declared by the API.
A field declaration is satisfied by
a (possibly implicit) getter and/or setter declaration,
depending on whether the field
is declared to be \KWD{hidden} and/or \KWD{settable}
by the exported declaration.

A method declaration is satisfied
by a set of method declarations
the union of whose parameter types
is the parameter type of the exported declaration,
and each of whose return types
is a subtype of the return type of the exported declaration.

# Rung C of climb batch 3: four comments in the interpreter library

- problem: explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47 (the closure's `NOT YET` comment, asked for "either way") and :44 (the `Array3` clause and the scalar block approved as landed: the `Array3` clause as landed is the explainer's option B at explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-19/library-findings-explained.md:193, whose default was A, :189 and :199, so Pavol's approval as landed chose B; the scalar block is on the explainer's defaults 3a-A and 3b-A at :249-255 and :272-283)

- precedent: Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1297, :1374, :1589-1590 (the `.fss` `NOT YET` form) and Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:818, :1063 (the `.fsi` `not yet:` form); Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4503 (the scalar block's own `(*)` header comment)

## 4. The specification, comment by comment

1. **The closure.** `Specification/basic/traits.tex:231-235` (a note box): the traits listed in a

The intersection of a set of types $S$ is equal to a named type $U$ when
any subtype of every type $T \in S$ and of the intersection of every
subset of $S$ is a subtype of $U$.
Similarly, the union of a set of types $S$ is equal to a named type $U$ when
any supertype of every type $T \in S$ and of the union of every
subset of $S$ is a supertype of $U$.

## The numeral defect measured by the first skeptic (home 2)

**What was measured.** The first skeptic rounded four numerals that lie within half an ulp of a tie but are not ties (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/SkNearTie.fss`). It ran them under `walk` before and after this rung's edit and on the compiled path. It also rounded the same four values written as quotients, which the library makes rationals (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/SkNearTieRational.fss`). The capture is `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/SkNearTie.txt`:

| numeral | `walk` before (`:8-11`) | `walk` after (`:2-5`) | compiled (`:15-18`) | specification, = `walk`'s rational body on the quotient (`:21-24`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2.50000000000000001` | 3 | 2 | 2 | 3 |
| `2.49999999999999999` | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| `3.49999999999999999` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 3 |
| `0.50000000000000001` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

The compiled column was measured after the edit. It is also the compiled answer before it, because the rung touches no file of the compiled path. The specification's answers are derived under "The specification" above: `literals.tex:162-163` makes each numeral a rational, and `numbers.tex:470-472` rounds it.

**What this rung does to it.** The rung did not create this defect and does not repair it. It changes three of `walk`'s four answers:

- two move away from the specification: `2.50000000000000001` goes 3 → 2, and `0.50000000000000001` goes 1 → 0;
- one moves toward it: `2.49999999999999999` goes 3 → 2;
- `3.49999999999999999` stays wrong at 4.

The first version of this report did not record this. The two answers the old `walk` had right were right by coincidence. The nearest double of both `2.50000000000000001` and `2.49999999999999999` is `2.5` itself, and the nearest double of `3.49999999999999999` is `3.5`. From the one double `2.5`, the specification wants 3 for the first numeral, 2 for the second and 2 for `2.5`. No rounding rule applied to the double can give all three: half up got the first right and the other two wrong, and half to even gets the last two right and the first wrong. So these numerals are not a reason to keep `Math.round`. The rule on the double is chosen where a double is exact: at `2.5` written as a numeral, the specification says half to even, and for a `Float` or `RR32` value the decision at `POSITIONS.md:49` says the same. The near-tie numerals have to be repaired one step earlier, where the numeral becomes a double.

**The mechanism.** This is the judge's section 2 (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/JUDGE.md`). I opened each of its citations:

- **The interpreter's library declares the numeral a floating-point value.** `object FloatLiteral extends RR64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:194`), and `trait RR64 extends Number comprises { Float, FloatLiteral, RR32, QQ }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:425`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:338`).
  - `object FloatLiteral` declares only `asString`, `asExprString` and `asFloat` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:195-200`). So its `floor`, `ceiling`, `truncate` and `round` are `trait Number`'s bodies over `asFloat(self)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:417`, `:419`, `:421`, `:422`).
  - `FloatLiteral$AsFloat` returns `FFloatLiteral.getFloat()`, which is `Double.valueOf` of the numeral's digits (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/FFloatLiteral.java:39-40`). Yet `FFloatLiteral` keeps a radix-ten numeral's digits exactly, as a `String` (`:17`, `:28`).
- **The interpreter has no coercion mechanism.** `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:288` records "no occurrence of `Coercion` or `coerce` anywhere under `interpreter/`". So the coercion to ℚ that `literals.tex:146-148` describes cannot exist in `walk` in the form the specification gives it.
- **The compiled prelude has no ℚ.** `QQ` occurs zero times in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi`, `CompilerBuiltin.fss`, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi` and `CompilerLibrary.fss`. The prelude declares `trait FloatLiteral excludes {RR32, RR64}` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:991`), and `trait RR64`'s `coerce(x: FloatLiteral) = x.asRR64` (`:927`) turns the numeral into a double before `RR64.round`.
- **The numeral types exist nowhere.** The types of `literals.tex:83-131`, such as `NaturalNumeral` and `RadixPointNumeral`, occur nowhere under `ProjectFortress/src`, `Library` or `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin` (grep, no hit). Ledger row 325 records the integer half of that absence.

So the defect is the compound-numeral half of a design-level gap: on both paths a numeral with a radix point is a floating-point value, not the rational the specification makes it. The four integer-valued methods are where the gap shows without a comparison of digits. The same cause also shows in comparison and arithmetic, which matters to the choice of repair below. Under `walk`:

- `2.50000000000000001 = 2.5` is `true`;
- `2.50000000000000001 - 2.5` is `0.0`;
- the same two values written as quotients compare unequal.

The capture is `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/NumeralAsDoubleProbe.txt:2-3` and `:5`.

**The gate.**

- `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss` is the first skeptic's proposal (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss`), with its one comment line pointed at this report. Its four assertions (`:7-10`) are the specification's answers, with the three that fail today first. Each message cites `literals.tex:162-163, numbers.tex:470-472`.
- **Today it is an expected failure.** Run directly, it stops at its first assertion with `FAIL: a Long: 2 =/= a Int: 3; numeral round(2.50000000000000001) = 3: …`, exit 1. Under `SystemJUTest` on a one-file copy, the harness prints ` OK Saw expected exception` and `OK (1 test)`. Capture: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/xxx-numeral-expected-failure.txt`.
  - The mechanics are `InterpreterTest`'s. Its expected-failure flag is `s.startsWith("XXX")` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:711`). A thrown failure then prints ` OK Saw expected exception` and returns (`:360-361`). A run that throws nothing prints ` Missing expected failure ` and fails the test (`:400-402`).
  - The shared prefix's `:922`, `:577`, `:644`, `:841` and `:843` point at other test classes' copies of the same logic, ten lines further down in this tree (`:932`, `:587`, `:654`, `:851`, `:853`), as the judge found.
- **Shown red on a deliberate local fix** (the judge's D2). I added a temporary `FloatLiteral$Round` to `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/FloatLiteral.java`: `FLong.make(new java.math.BigDecimal(x.getString()).setScale(0, java.math.RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN).longValueExact())`. It was bound in `object FloatLiteral` by `round(self): ZZ64 = builtinPrimitive("…FloatLiteral$Round")`, followed by `ant compileAll` and wiped caches. With the fix in:
  - the XXX file prints `PASS`, exit 0;
  - the harness prints ` Missing expected failure ` and `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0`, exit 1;
  - `SkNearTie.fss` gives 3, 2, 3 and 1, the specification's four answers;
  - `SkNearIntNumeral.fss` still gives `3.0`, `2.0` and `3`.

  Capture: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/xxx-numeral-red-on-deliberate-fix.txt`, which also carries the fix's diff.
- **Reverted.** I ran `git checkout --` on the two files, `ant compileAll` again, and wiped the caches again. Then:
  - `git status` lists neither file;
  - the build has no `FloatLiteral$Round` class, and `Float$Round` still calls `rint`;
  - the XXX file fails again, exit 1, and the harness prints ` OK Saw expected exception`;
  - `RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss` prints `PASS`, exit 0.

  Capture: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/xxx-numeral-after-revert.txt`.

  The fix is in no commit: `git diff --stat d610695c0...HEAD` lists `Float.java`, `RR32.java`, the two test files and this directory.

**Two decisions, the judge's, executed here** (`JUDGE.md` section 4):

- **D1: one `XXX` file, on `round` only.** `floor`, `ceiling` and `truncate` on a numeral are the same defect, with one cause and one repair under every candidate. The provisional row names them, with `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/SkNearIntNumeral.txt`.
  - Reason: an `XXX` file flips only when every assertion in it passes. A file that also carried the other three methods would stay red through a `round`-only repair and say nothing.
  - The deliberate fix confirms the premise: with `round` repaired alone, `SkNearIntNumeral`'s three answers stay wrong.
  - Alternative rejected: a second `XXX` file for the three methods (`testSystem` 387). It would guard only against a repair of `floor` that leaves `round` alone.
  - This is a decision under the batch's home-2 rule, not under the specification.
- **D2: the deliberate fix is a real temporary native, not a swap of the asserted values.** A real native also shows that the assertions are reachable through `object FloatLiteral`'s own dispatch, and that the `FLong`-against-`IntLiteral` comparison passes when the value is right. It cost one `ant compileAll` each way (28 s and 27 s).

**The fork on the repair: Pavol's decision, and the row's fix column.** This is `JUDGE.md` section 5.2, with one correction:

- **(a) The narrow patch.** `object FloatLiteral` gets `round`, `floor`, `ceiling` and `truncate` over the exact decimal: `BigDecimal` of the digits `FFloatLiteral` keeps, with `HALF_EVEN`, `FLOOR`, `CEILING` and `DOWN`. That goes into `walk` now, and onto the compiled side with the one library at the switch-over.
  - Cost: about 30 lines and a rebuild.
  - The numeral then rounds as a rational but still compares and subtracts as a double (`NumeralAsDoubleProbe.txt:2-3`), an inconsistency inside one value.
  - The return types interact with row 330's decision (ℤ).
  - The correction: the judge's text says the numeral would also print as a double. It does not. `FloatLiteral$ToString` returns the numeral's own digits (`glue/prim/FloatLiteral.java:49-53`, bound at `FortressBuiltin.fss:195-196`), and `2.50000000000000001` prints as written (`NumeralAsDoubleProbe.txt:4`).
- **(b) The design.** A compound numeral becomes a rational value, as `literals.tex:146-148` and `:162-163` say. Either `FloatLiteral` leaves `RR64` for ℚ (`FortressLibrary.fss:425`, `FortressBuiltin.fss:194`), or the one library gets the specification's coercion once the checker's coercion machinery runs on the library route. Cost:
  - every float expression that mentions a literal goes through exact rational arithmetic and one conversion, which `literals.tex:170-173` allows;
  - the hot float paths of rows 302 and 303;
  - `List[\FloatLiteral\]` inference (row 20);
  - `FFloatLiteral.seqv`;
  - ℚ is absent from the compiler prelude until the one library;
  - the checker's numeral typing (row 325) is the static half of the same design.
- **(c) The team's design stands.** A compound numeral is an `RR64` value, recorded in `POSITIONS.md` as a decision against the prose. Then the `XXX` file is deleted and the row closes as design.

The rung does not wait on this. The gate is right under (a) and (b), because both make its four assertions pass, and it is removed under (c).

- Walk before gives 3 and 1 on the two ties whose lower neighbour is even (`Sk2RR32Arith.txt`).
   - **Rule 4.** The same as probe 1.
3. **`probes/skeptic/Sk2Radix.fss`.** Radix-point numerals with an explicit radix other than ten: `10.1_2` (5/2), `11.1_2` (7/2), `0.8_16` (1/2), `2.8_16` (5/2), and `10.1000…0001_2` (5/2 + 2⁻⁵⁶).

   - Walk before gives 3, 4, 1, 3, 3 (`:10-14`).
   - **Rule 4 for the four exact ties.** The specification settles them, and the compiled path was right. `literals.tex:117-125` gives such a numeral its value in radix r, and with `:162-163` and `numbers.tex:470-472` the answers are 2, 4, 0 and 2. The rung repairs `walk`.
   - **Rule 4 for the fifth.** The fifth is a near tie. The specification's answer is 3, and both paths give 2. That is provisional row 354's defect (the fourth outcome), and the rung moved `walk` from 3 to 2 on it.
   - Under `walk` that numeral prints `2.5` (`:7`). `FFloatLiteral`'s constructor keeps a double's rendering, not the digits, whenever the radix is not ten (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/FFloatLiteral.java:28-32`).
   - The compiled run then throws on the print line; see recommended row B.
4. **`probes/skeptic/Sk2NegNumeral.fss`.** It rounds `-2.50000000000000001`, `-0.50000000000000001`, `2.5 + 0.00000000000000001`, `-2.5`, `-0.5` and `-3.5`, and prints the negated near tie.
   - Walk after and compiled agree on the six rounds, −2, 0, 2, −2, 0 and −4 (`Sk2NegNumeral.txt:2-7`, `:23-28`). The negated value prints `-2.5` on both paths (`:8`, `:29`).
   - Walk before differs on two lines. `2.5 + 0.00000000000000001` gave 3 (`:14`), and `-3.5` gave −3 (`:17`).
   - **Rule 4 for the three ties.** The specification settles them: a numeral is a rational (`literals.tex:162-163`), rational arithmetic is exact (`:157-158`), and the tie goes to the even integer. The answers are −2, 0 and −4. Both paths are now right.
   - **Rule 4 for the three near-tie expressions.** The specification's answers are −3, −1 and 3, and both paths give −2, 0 and 2. That is row 354's defect again, the fourth outcome.
   - The two negated near ties were wrong before the rung as well. `2.5 + 0.00000000000000001` moved from 3 (right by the coincidence the report describes) to 2.
5. **`probes/skeptic/Sk2RadixTen.fss`.** `round(2.5_10)` and `round(3.5_10)`: a radix-point numeral with the explicit radix specifier `_10`.
   - `walk` throws `NumberFormatException: For input string: "2.5_10"` at `FFloatLiteral.getFloat` (`FFloatLiteral.java:40`), both before and after the edit.
   - The compiled path answers 2 and 4 (`Sk2RadixTen.txt:17`, `:110`, `:189-190`).
   - **Rule 4.** The specification settles it against `walk`. `lexical-structure.tex:1083-1095` makes `_10` a valid radix specifier naming radix ten, and `literals.tex:117-125` with `:162-163` gives the numeral the value 5/2. This is outcome two: a ledger row is owed against the interpreter.
   - It is not the rung's construct. The throw happens in `asFloat` before `round` is reached, and the rung changes nothing about it. This is recommended row A.
   - A proposed home-2 gate is `probes/skeptic/XXXRadixTenPointNumeral.fss`. It is red today and prints ` OK Saw expected exception` under `SystemJUTest` (`SkXXXRadixTen-harness.txt`). Its comment line points here, so whoever places it repoints the line at that rung's `REPORT.md`.
6. **`probes/skeptic/Sk2NumeralPrint.fss`.** It prints a typed `RR64` binding, `println(2.5)` and `"…" 2.5`.
   - `walk` prints `2.5` three times.
   - The compiled path prints the binding, then throws `NullPointerException` at `println(2.5)` (`Sk2NumeralPrint.txt:21-23`), because `CompilerBuiltin$Object.asString()` is null. `Sk2NegNumeral.txt:30` and `Sk2Radix.txt:24` hit the same throw.
   - The prose is silent on how a numeral renders. This is recommended row B.

## The failure-mode question

The rung replaces no loud failure.
- `Math.round(double)` and `(long) Math.rint(double)` are both total. NaN gives 0 either way: `Math.round` by its contract, and `(long)` of NaN by JLS §5.1.3. ±∞ and values of magnitude 2^63 or more saturate to 2^63−1 and −2^63 either way.
- The worker's probe pair (`probes/RoundHalfEvenWalkProbe-before.txt` against `-after.txt`) and `probes/RoundHalfEvenCompiledProbe.txt` show NaN, ±∞ and ±`exp(100)` unchanged before, after and compiled, and the first skeptic reproduced them.
- The only change is at an exact tie whose lower neighbour is even, where one quiet integer replaces another.
- The two loud failures I met, `2.5_10` under `walk` and a printed numeral on the compiled path, are not this rung's. It changes neither.

## Required correction: provisional row 354 must state what candidate (a) does not reach

**The problem.** The row, and the fork in `REPORT.md`, describe candidate (a) as `object FloatLiteral` getting `round`, `floor`, `ceiling` and `truncate` over "`BigDecimal` of the digits `FFloatLiteral` keeps". Then they say "the gate is right under (a) and (b), because both make its four assertions pass". The second sentence is true. But (a) repairs only a bare radix-ten numeral, and three measured faces of the same defect stay wrong under it:

- **A negated numeral and arithmetic on numerals.** These are a `Float` before `round` runs. `trait Number`'s `opr -(self):RR64 = -asFloat(self)` and `opr +(self,b:Number):RR64 = asFloat(self) + asFloat(b)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:378-379`) convert first, and `-2.50000000000000001` prints `-2.5` (`Sk2NegNumeral.txt:8`). A method on `object FloatLiteral` is never selected for these values. Measured on both paths after rung R:

  | expression | both paths | specification |
  |---|---|---|
  | `round(-2.50000000000000001)` | −2 | −3 |
  | `round(-0.50000000000000001)` | 0 | −1 |
  | `round(2.5 + 0.00000000000000001)` | 2 | 3 |

  The specification's answers follow from `literals.tex:157-158` (rational arithmetic is exact) and `:162-163`.
- **A numeral with a radix other than ten.** It has lost its digits when it is built (`FFloatLiteral.java:28-32`), and it prints `2.5` (`Sk2Radix.txt:7`). So `BigDecimal` of what `FFloatLiteral` keeps is a double's rendering. Measured: `round(10.1000…0001_2)` is 2 on both paths, and the specification says 3 (`literals.tex:117-125`, `:162-163`).

Under (a), then, `XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss` would flip and turn the suite red, while these four expressions stay wrong. The flip would not mean that row 354 is closed. Pavol is choosing between (a), (b) and (c) on this text, so it has to say so.

**What to add**, to the provisional row's notes in `record.md` and to the fork in `REPORT.md` ("The numeral defect measured by the first skeptic"):

1. The four expressions above, with their values on both paths and the specification's, citing `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/Sk2NegNumeral.txt` and `Sk2Radix.txt`.
2. One sentence under (a): it reaches only a bare radix-ten numeral, because a negated or summed numeral is already a `Float` (`FortressLibrary.fss:378-379`) and a numeral with another radix keeps no digits (`FFloatLiteral.java:28-32`). Under (a) the `XXX` file's flip therefore does not close the row. Whoever lands (a) adds an `XXX` file for these forms or narrows the row by recorded decision.
3. In the sentence that lists the answers rung R moved away from the specification, add `2.5 + 0.00000000000000001` (3 → 2) and `10.1000…0001_2` (3 → 2).
4. Qualify the correction to the judge's candidate (a) at `REPORT.md:228`, "prints its own digits", as true of a radix-ten numeral only.

The claim of candidate (b) is unaffected: a rational numeral makes every one of these the rational's answer. So is candidate (c).

## Other findings, not required

- **D1 still stands for `floor`, `ceiling` and `truncate`.** Candidate (a) adds all four methods, so its premise holds for them. It does not hold for the three faces above, which is why the correction is to the row's text and not to D1.

## Recommended rows

These are for the gather to open or refuse. Neither is this rung's to repair.

- **A.** `walk` throws `NumberFormatException` on any floating-point use of a radix-point numeral with an explicit radix-ten specifier (`2.5_10`), where the compiled path answers.
- **B.** The compiled path throws `NullPointerException` when it prints a floating-point numeral (`println(2.5)`), where `walk` prints it. `FFloatLiteral.asString` is the one remaining `return null` among the runtime values, and the team has already repaired its `FIntLiteral` twin.

The proposed row text is in this judgement's structured output. Both rows cite the captures above.

## What changed

- `nativeHelpers/stringOps.java:48-72`: `typeName(fortress.AnyType.Any a)` and its private helper `fortressTypeName(String)`, unchanged in the repair round. `typeName` reads `a.getClass().getName()`, applies `Naming.dotToSep` and `Naming.demangleFortressIdentifier`, and renders: the segment after the last `/` or `$` of the stem; the leading `F` dropped from a class in `com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/` (`:58`); static arguments split by `RTHelpers.extractStringParameters` and rendered recursively inside `[\ \]` with `,`; a `Tuple`/`ConcreteTuple` stem as `(A,B)`; an `Arrow`/`AbstractArrow` stem as `A->B`, parenthesizing the domain only when the stem carries more than one input; `☃` as `()` (`:54`).
- `nativeHelpers/stringOps.java:74-86` (the repair round): the bound native `defaultAsString(fortress.AnyType.Any a)`, `return hasOwnToString(a) ? a.toString() : typeName(a);` (`:75-77`), under a one-line descriptive comment (`:74`), and the private `hasOwnToString(fortress.AnyType.Any a)` (`:79-86`), true when `a.getClass().getMethod("toString").getDeclaringClass()` is neither `FValue.class` nor `Object.class`, false on `NoSuchMethodException`. With the import lines at `:14-18` (`java.util.List`, `compiler.runtimeValues.FValue` added in the repair round, `Naming`, `RTHelpers`), 44 lines against the base.
- `LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:283`: `stringOps.defaultAsString => jDefaultAsString}` added to the `stringOps` import (the rung tree's `stringOps.typeName => jTypeName` replaced; `jTypeName` is no longer imported).
- `LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:351` (base `:350`): `getter asString(): String = jAsString(self)` became `= jDefaultAsString(self)`.
- Unchanged on purpose: `FValue.toString` (`compiler/runtimeValues/FValue.java:25-27`) stays `this.asString().toString()`. For a class that declares a `toString` of its own, the default `asString` answers that `toString`; for every generated class `toString` resolves to `FValue`'s (codegen defines none: `grep -rn '"toString"' compiler/ runtimeSystem/` finds only calls, `CodeGen.java:2108` on a `StringBuilder` and `environments/TopLevelEnvGen.java:625` in the interpreter's environment classes) and is `this.asString().toString()`, the type name. So a Java caller's `toString()` of a value whose `asString` is this default shows what `println` shows, on every class. `asDebugString` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:353`) stays `self.asString`; `stringOps.asString` and its `jAsString` import stay (see Decisions).
- Tests, all in the gated corpora: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/DefaultRenderRungS.fss` + `.test` (the gated test, 18 assertions); the expected-failure pairs `XXXJuxtConcatRungS` (row 76), `XXXUnionReturnRungS`, `XXXOprParamRungS`, `XXXNatArgRungS` in `compiler_tests/`, each an `XXX<Name>.fss` + `XXX<Name>.test` + `<Name>Link.test`; `compiler_tests/XXXUnionMethodRungS.fss` + `.test` (compile stage only); and `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXInferredStaticArgRungS.fss` (interpreter, no `.test` file). See "Defects and their homes".

What a compiled program prints now: `Box`, `Cell[\ZZ32\]`, `Pt`, `Two[\ZZ32,String\]`, `Cell[\Cell[\ZZ32\]\]`, `AnyCell[\(ZZ32,String)\]`, `AnyCell[\ZZ32->ZZ32\]`, `AnyCell[\(ZZ32,ZZ32)->ZZ32\]`, `Tag[\()\]`, `Tag[\()->ZZ32\]`; the compiled prelude's objects with no `asString` of their own print their names instead of overflowing: `None` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:1451`), `Infinity`, `NegativeInfinity`, `IndefiniteNumber` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:509-511`), `Nothing` (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:580`) and the reduction objects `StringConcatenation`, `ZZ32Addition`, `ZZ32Max` (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:458`, `:463`, `:468`) — every `object` declaration in the five compiled prelude components with no `getter asString` before its `end`. And the two natively implemented traits whose values reach the default print what they printed on the base tree: an `RR32` value its Java rendering, `1.5` (`compiler/runtimeValues/FRR32.java:19`, `"" + val`), and a `StringVector` its Java rendering, `[a b ]` (`FStringVector.java:24-30`; its `asSring` at `:34` is misspelled and so is no `asString`).

## Precedent search

- **Rendering a type name: one way, the interpreter's.** `FObject.toString` is `type().toString()` (`interpreter/evaluator/values/FObject.java:33-39`); a generic instance appends `Useful.listInOxfords` of its arguments (`interpreter/evaluator/types/FTraitOrObject.java:184-191`, `useful/Useful.java:233-235`, separator `","` at `:79-80`); a tuple type is `Useful.listInParens` (`FTypeTuple.java:61-63`) and an arrow `domain + "->" + range` (`FTypeArrow.java:107-109`). The interpreter's own `toString` is `asString`: `getter toString(): String = self.asString (* deprecated *)` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:51`), which is what makes the specification's `toString` contract the contract of `asString`. The compiled path had no type-name rendering; the native reproduces the interpreter's, and the differentials below show it byte for byte.
- **Decoding a stamped class name: two ways, both followed.** `RTTI.className()` (`RTTI.java:53-58`: canonical name, `demangleFortressIdentifier`, `dotToSep`) and the class loader's decode of a generic class name (`runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:246-251`: `dotToSep`, `demangleFortressIdentifier`, the stem before `⟦`, `RTHelpers.extractStringParameters`) followed by a dispatch on the *full* stem against `Naming.ARROW_TAG`, `ABSTRACT_ARROW`, `WRAPPED_ARROW`, `Naming.TUPLE_TAG`, `CONCRETE_TUPLE`, `ANY_TUPLE`, `ANY_CONCRETE_TUPLE`, `Naming.UNION` (`:252-269`). The native takes the class loader's order, reuses the public `RTHelpers.extractStringParameters(String)` (`RTHelpers.java:228-232`), and compares full stems as the class loader does, so a user object named `Tuple` (stem `Comp$Tuple`) is not taken for a tuple. `demangleFortressIdentifier` has 11 call sites in `src/com/sun/fortress/` (`InstantiationMap.java:35,48,67`, `RTHelpers.java:25`, `InstantiatingClassloader.java:236,244,247,284,1968,1974`, `RTTI.java:55`); none renders for a person.
- **A run-time class back to a Fortress name: none in the tree.** `Naming.specialFortressTypes` (`runtimeSystem/Naming.java:277`, filled at `:287-305`) maps the other way, is package-private, and lacks `NN32`, `NN64`, `String` and `IntLiteral`. The rule the native uses was measured instead: every value class in `compiler/runtimeValues/` is `F` followed by its Fortress name, for all 17 of them (`FBoolean`, `FCharacter`, `FFloatLiteral`, `FIntLiteral`, `FJavaBufferedReader`, `FJavaBufferedWriter`, `FJavaString`, `FNN32`, `FNN64`, `FRR32`, `FRR64`, `FString`, `FStringVector`, `FZZ`, `FZZ32`, `FZZ32Vector`, `FZZ64`); `FVoid` never appears, because `VoidRTTI.className()` is `☃` (`VoidRTTI.java:18-20`).
- **The same defect elsewhere.** A native `asString` that calls `toString()` on a Fortress value closes the cycle unless the value's class overrides `toString`. Five natives call `toString()` on an argument: `stringOps.asString` (`stringOps.java:43-46`), `simpleIntVector.asString` (`simpleIntVector.java:17`), `fileOps.jbrAsString` and `jbwAsString` (`fileOps.java:41-43`, `:86-88`) and `simpleIntLiteralArith.toBigInteger` (`simpleIntLiteralArith.java:15-17`). The other four take classes that define their own `toString` (`FZZ32Vector.java:29`, `FortressBufferedReader.java:34`, `FortressBufferedWriter.java:34`, `FIntLiteral.java:52`), so the cycle had one site, the one repaired. `FException`'s two `asString()` calls (`FException.java:23`, `:31`) are entries into it, not sites of it.
- **The reverse count, which the repaired defect raises.** Of the 17 value classes, 2 relied on the old default reaching their own `toString`, because neither their trait nor their Java class has an `asString`: `FRR32` (`FRR32.java:19`) and `FStringVector` (`FStringVector.java:24-30`). The other 15 have an `asString` at one level or the other (Java: `FFloatLiteral`, `FIntLiteral`, `FNN32`, `FRR64`, `FString`, `FZZ32`, `FZZ32Vector`; trait only: `FBoolean` `CompilerBuiltin.fss:1006`, `FCharacter` `:1061`, `FJavaBufferedReader` `:1158`, `FJavaBufferedWriter` `:1172`, `FJavaString` `:419`, `FNN64` `:821`, `FZZ` `:519`, `FZZ64` `:580`). The first round asked the forward question only; `defaultAsString` answers both.
- **A private helper in an imported native class.** Every one found has a Fortress-mappable signature (listed in "The repair round"), which is why `hasOwnToString` takes the value.

## Defects and their homes

1. **Row 321, the rendering cycle** — home 1, repaired. Its assertions are the 18 `assert` lines of `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/DefaultRenderRungS.fss:21-48`, each message carrying "ledger row 321" (the last also `FException.java:22-23`). They cover the entry points the row names that a test can reach: `println` (`:18-20`, checked by `run_out_contains=PASS` reaching `:49`), concatenation (`:33`), the prelude singletons `Nothing` and `None` (`:34-35`), and a `throw` of an object with no `asString` reaching its handler (`:42-48`). The transactional entry is gated already by `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelObjectVar`, which passes on the repaired tree (`probes/gated-spot-postrepair.txt:3-10`).
2. **The void, tuple and arrow spellings** — home 1: in the native and asserted at `DefaultRenderRungS.fss:27-32`.
3. **`RR32` and `StringVector` values rendered as their type name** (the skeptic's, introduced by the rung's first native) — home 1, repaired in this round: `DefaultRenderRungS.fss:36-41`, failing before the repair (`probes/test-prerepair.txt:11`), passing after (`probes/test-postedit.txt:10-15`), biting under mutation (`probes/mutation-owntostring.txt:17`). `objects.tex:117-122` settles it.
4. **`asDebugString` diverges between the paths** — home 3, provisional ledger row 354. Walk prints `a Box: Box` (article + `ilkName` + `": "` + `asString`, `FortressBuiltin.fss:42-47`), the compiled path `Box` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:353` is `self.asString`). The specification's prose never names `asDebugString`, `asExprString` or `ilkName` (`grep -rn 'asExprString\|asDebugString\|ilkName' Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` prints nothing, rc=1, re-run in this round), so this is the home for a silent specification, not a choice of convenience; the batch record keeps the repair out of this rung because `not_working_library_tests/Comparison1.fss:33-36` asserts `U.asDebugString = "Unordered"`. Probe: `probes/judgement-probes-both-paths.txt`. The gated test asserts nothing about `asDebugString`.
5. **`asExprString` diverges between the paths** (the skeptic's) — home 3, an addition to row 354, for the same reason: the prose is silent (the grep above). Walk prints `no expression for Circ` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:48-49`); the compiled path prints `[no expression for  Circ ]`, brackets from `CompilerBuiltin.fss:352` and the doubled spaces from row 76. It overflowed the stack before the rung, so a loud failure became a quiet divergent value. Probe `probes/skeptic/SkTraitTyped.fss`; captures `probes/skeptic/differentials.txt:46`, `:54`, and on the repaired tree `probes/postrepair-differentials.txt:44`.
6. **Row 76, string juxtaposition inserts spaces on the compiled path** — home 2, an expected-failure test. The specification settles it: with a string on the left, juxtaposition "conventionally performs string concatenation" (`Specification/basic/operators/intro.tex:68-70`, read `:50-76`), and string concatenation is `||` with no separator (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:75-79`, read `:65-95`); `juxtameaning.tex:103-105` makes `"<" Box(1) ">"` legal. The compiled prelude defines `opr juxtaposition(self, b:Object): String = self ||| b` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:402`), and `|||` inserts a space (`nativeHelpers/simpleConcatenate.java:20-24`). The repair changes the output of nearly every compiled program that prints and the prelude is frozen, so it is gated as `compiler_tests/XXXJuxtConcatRungS.fss` with `XXXJuxtConcatRungS.test` (`run`, `run_out_contains=REACHED`) and `JuxtConcatRungSLink.test` (`link`), split as rung B split `XXXClauseBindingRungB` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-tryatomic/REPORT.md:287-320`; `FileTests.java:605`, `:587-591`). It fails as expected on the base, rung and repaired trees (`probes/xxx-juxt-preedit.txt:22`, `probes/xxx-juxt-postedit.txt:20`), and was shown to go red on a fix (`probes/xxx-juxt-goes-red.txt:16`, `:23`).

The numeral case (`Cell(3)`: walk `Cell[\Int\]`, compiled `Cell[\IntLiteral\]`) is not asserted: a numeral has type `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]` (`literals.tex:84-86`), which neither path implements; it is in the row's text only.

9. **An object with an `opr` static parameter cannot be instantiated on the compiled path** (the skeptic's) — home 2, `compiler_tests/XXXOprParamRungS.fss` + `.test` + `OprParamRungSLink.test`, provisional row 357. `trait-parameters.tex:156-176` (read `:145-178`) specifies operator parameters and their instantiation as static arguments. The adapter wraps every method of the class (`FortressMethodAdapter.java:215-225`), a private method cannot be imported, and the error names no method (`probes/judge-shape-wrapper-error.txt:6`). Approved, with two required corrections.

The repair does what my first refusal asked. `stringOps.defaultAsString` (`stringOps.java:75-77`) returns a value's own Java `toString` when its class declares one, and the type name otherwise. `RR32` prints `1.5` and `StringVector` prints `[a b ]` again, and two assertions in the gated test cover them (`DefaultRenderRungS.fss:37,41`).

The recorded failure is genuine and was taken test first: commit `75741de9a` adds only the assertions and the capture, while `typeName` is still bound (`probes/test-prerepair.txt:11`).

I re-checked everything on a cache I wiped and rebuilt myself:
- The 18 assertions pass.
- All ten `.test` files and the interpreter expected failure behave as claimed.
- The five-line provenance block's citations all say what the block says.
- The `record.md` texts for rows 76, 307 and 354-359 check out.
- The ladder subset is byte-identical.

This round I measured one new defect. An object that declares or inherits a zero-argument Fortress member named `toString` (a method, a getter or a field) still overflows the stack:
- Codegen emits that member as `toString()Lfortress/CompilerBuiltin$String;`.
- `Class.getMethod("toString")` returns a method the class declares itself before any inherited one, so `hasOwnToString` (`:79-86`) answers true.
- `a.toString()` then resolves to `FValue.toString`, which re-enters the default at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:351`.

Walk prints the type name for these objects. The base tree overflowed on them too, so this is not a regression from the base. It stays a loud failure, and no program in the gated corpora or the compiled prelude has this shape. A five-line fix, which only counts a `toString` that returns `java.lang.String`, was verified as a stand-in: the four probes print the type name and `DefaultRenderRungS` still passes.

That makes the rung improvable rather than wrong, so I did not refuse a second time. Under the three-homes rule the defect cannot be repaired after this judgement, so it goes to home 2. I wrote an expected-failure pair and verified it: link OK today, run 'Saw expected failure' today, red on the stand-in fix, and back to expected after the restore. The commit stage must land that pair, and the record must stop saying row 321 is fully repaired.

Findings are in `/home/user/fortress-rendering/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-default-rendering/SKEPTIC.md` (second judgement appended from line 141). Probes and captures are in `/home/user/fortress-rendering/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-default-rendering/probes/skeptic/` (the `Sk2*.fss` probes, the `skeptic2-*.txt` captures and `proposed/`). They are committed as `51d3b3ac6` and pushed to `wip/rung-default-rendering`.
----
* The refusal is repaired. defaultAsString (stringOps.java:75-77) keeps a class's own Java toString and otherwise returns typeName. RR32 prints 1.5 and StringVector prints [a b ] (skeptic2-differentials.txt:141-151), asserted at DefaultRenderRungS.fss:37,41, and all 18 assertions pass on the skeptic's own rebuilt cache (skeptic2-gated-tests.txt:2-10).

* The recorded failure exists and was taken test first. Commit 75741de9a adds only the two assertions and probes/test-prerepair.txt; at that commit CompilerBuiltin.fss:283/:351 still bind jTypeName and there is no defaultAsString. The failing line is :11 (FAIL:  RR32 =/= 1.5) and :37 has Tests run: 2, Failures: 1.

* The provenance block has five lines and every citation matches: problem, spec (basic-lib only, grep rc=1), precedent, deviation (now one line), and historical (stringOps.java and CompilerBuiltin.fss are the only 2012-tree files modified). The trailing '— none' on the spec line is stray.

* New defect: an object that declares or inherits a zero-argument Fortress member named toString (method, getter, field, or a trait's) still overflows the stack on the compiled path. Codegen emits it as 'public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String toString()' (skeptic2-overflow-cycle.txt:8). Class.getMethod("toString") returns that declared method, so hasOwnToString (stringOps.java:79-86) answers true, and a.toString() at :76 resolves to FValue.toString, which re-enters CompilerBuiltin.fss:351 (the cycle is at :33-40). Walk prints Foo, Bar, Qux and Rec. The base tree also overflowed, so this is no regression from the base; the refused first-round tree printed the type name.

* The judge's safety argument (JUDGE.md section 3) and REPORT.md:17 rest on a grep for the literal "toString" in codegen. That grep cannot see a Java method that codegen names after a Fortress declaration. The team's interpreter library declares such members (Generator22D.fss:64,107,172; Generator2.fsi:61,70; FortressLibrary.fsi:1841,1849), and the interpreter's trait Object declares getter toString (FortressBuiltin.fss:51). Adopting that Object at the switch-over would make every object recurse unless the detection is fixed first.

* A fix is verified as a stand-in: walk the superclass chain below FValue and count only a declared no-argument toString that returns java.lang.String. The four probes then print the type name and DefaultRenderRungS still passes 18/18 (skeptic2-standin-fix.txt:18-61). It is not applied, because the three-homes rule needs a home-1 assertion in place before the second skeptic runs.
